thread.title: Apple: It Likely Gets Worse - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Bill Maurer
title: Apple: It Likely Gets Worse - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Last week, I encouraged investors to wait until the dust settled for technology giant Apple ( AAPL ). After the company's major revenue warning for the holiday quarter spooked investors, shares have recovered a bit from their recent lows. Unfortunately, none of the major short term risks have cleared, meaning we likely need more time for the situation to resolve itself.
( Source: Yahoo! Finance)
You could say that there were two major strikeouts last week. On the trade front, there was no major announcement between the U.S. and China, only "further talks" that will continue moving forward. While I don't know if additional tariffs will be implemented once we hit the previous 3-month deadline, the lack of a deal likely means China's economy struggles further in early 2019. With the company's new year coming up, a further push from consumers against Apple products will likely impact results. As I detailed in my article last week, Apple faces a tougher bar in the March 2019 quarter from China's previous year results than it did in the December 2018 one.
The second major issue is the U.S. government shutdown. Now more than three weeks into the process, we finally hit the point last Friday where employees are starting to miss their paychecks. The U.S. economy will likely see a small hit in Q1 as a result, and we've already seen areas of the economy like housing be negatively impacted by rising rates. With markets well off their highs and seeing increased volatility, consumers may just tighten their wallets a bit.
The other major problem is a flow through impact. As I discussed a number of months ago, Apple management made a decision in 2018 to prioritize margins over market share . This sent device pricing higher across the iPhone, Mac, and iPad lines, to the point where unit sales have suffered. While average selling prices have surged, less unit sales means less accessories sales and lower potential for add-on services. Just take a look at Gartner which believes Mac unit sales dipped in calendar Q4 2018. It wouldn't surprise me if iPhone units declined year over year when Apple reports in a couple of weeks.
If you sell a few million fewer units, there's a smaller crowd for things like Apple Care, Apple Pay, Apple Music, etc. While Apple eventually will launch a streaming service to help the Services segment, that's likely not going to impact results anytime soon. Additionally, as I pointed out in my prior article, the accounting change Apple made makes the year ago Services numbers a bit higher, averaging more than $600 million more in revenues per quarter. Take a look at what that does to the 2018 fiscal quarter growth rates against their prior year counterparts.
( Source: Apple adjustment sheet and quarterly results page)
The accounting change basically adds 850 extra basis points of growth to last year's numbers, meaning investors are in for what could be a shocking slowdown early this year. If you remember from the recent revenue warning , the Services segment generated over $10.8 billion in revenue for the period. Against the year ago reported number, that would mean 27.5% growth, but thanks to the accounting change, growth is now just 18.3%. Just imagine what the numbers will be like in Q2 and Q3 with those much higher comps.
With unit sales likely coming up a bit short of previous expectations, Apple is likely to be more aggressive in its promotions to drive sales. The company had offered higher trade-in values during Q4 to begin with, but this doesn't seem to have done a lot of good. Apple is also reportedly cutting prices for vendors in China to make up for a sales shortfall there , which means we should see some margin compression during Q2. These trends usually take a couple of quarters to work themselves out. Don't forget, calendar Q1 2019 is the first period where Apple laps the U.S. tax cuts, meanings earnings per share face a much higher bar even considering the help from the buyback.
I still think we need to see estimates come down a little more for the March quarter. These revenue cycles usually take a couple of quarters to turn, and with tougher year ago comparisons, I don't see how Q2 sees revenue growth acceleration of almost 200 basis points as currently expected. If I were looking for Apple to bottom, I'd be much happier with the street looking for a 5% to 10% revenue decline in the period, which is quite a bit below where we are now as seen below.
( Source: Yahoo! Finance analyst estimates page)
While Apple shares have bounced a bit off their recent lows, I still think we are a bit away from seeing a true bottom. With no trade deal reached yet between the U.S. and China, along with the U.S. government shutdown, consumer spending in the company's two key markets will struggle a little. Normally, iPhone unit sales slowdowns take a few quarters to work through, which means lower services growth for this quarter and next which face much high year ago comparison bars. I mentioned previously that selling below market puts would be my preferred strategy, as we likely need to see future estimates come down a little more. Let's see another quarter get into the books, as the stock will likely become more interesting ahead of a capital return update in April/May.
